profiles.summary: The two unexplained release notes of November 2026 are now identified from the tagged source. The mainnet node still reports tempo/v1.19.0-697ea97, and the interpreter revision has not changed since v1.18.3. A differential of 32 nested call cases gave byte identical results on Tempo and on Arc.

deltas.delta: Release v1.17.0 executed with revm 43.0.3. Release v1.18.2 moved to evm2 at revision a29a283f with a patch revision fc6acade, which the manifest describes as the perf-call branch. The difference between the two revisions in crates/evm2/src/evm/mod.rs makes the input of a call a range of the caller frame's memory in place of a copy (message.input.make_owned before inspector hooks, interp_ref.lend_memory when a frame starts). This is the item the release notes call EVM call input hardening.

At the mainnet revision 66687c18 the borrowed input is stored as a byte range plus the entry number of the caller frame and is resolved through the caller's memory when read (MessageInput, crates/evm2/src/interpreter/message.rs lines 209 to 313, and message_input in evm/mod.rs). A child frame that grows its own memory therefore cannot move the bytes it reads as calldata.

Releases v1.18.3, v1.18.4 and v1.19.0 pin the same evm2 revision 66687c18, and Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock of v1.18.3 and v1.18.4 differ only in the version number. Of 147 modules of crates/evm, crates/precompiles, crates/primitives, crates/transaction-pool, crates/payload/builder, crates/hardfork and crates/chainspec, two differ between the tags. crates/precompiles/src/lib.rs gains has_input_gas, and the precompile provider now returns an out of gas halt when the remaining gas does not cover the input cost, before it copies the borrowed input out of the caller's memory. crates/evm/src/instructions.rs applies the same check in the instruction that runs the T14 account marker. This is the fix for EVM execution of v1.18.4. For the PoolManager it means a call to a TIP-20 precompile with 36 or 68 bytes of input fails only when the gas left is below the input cost, a state in which the call could not complete anyway.
deltas.source: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/refs/tags/tempo/v1.18.3/crates/precompiles/src/lib.rs compared with https://raw.githubusercontent.com/tempoxyz/tempo/refs/tags/tempo/v1.18.4/crates/precompiles/src/lib.rs, and crates/evm/src/instructions.rs at the same two tags

deltas.delta: Differential for the borrowed input: three override contracts (a top frame, a middle frame that calls on with input and output on one range, and an echo frame that grows its memory to 64 kB before it copies its calldata), 8 input lengths from 1 to 1,000 bytes and 4 output offsets (same range, shifted by 16 and by 32 bytes, disjoint), followed by a STATICCALL on the same range after the memory was rewritten. All 32 results of 24,576 bytes each are identical on the Tempo endpoint (evm2) and on an Arc endpoint (revm 38).

profiles.summary: The four pooled tokens with value are native USDC under two ids, EURC, cirBTC and bridged WETH. findings.title: One USDC blocklist entry for the PoolManager on Arc stops native USDC in both directions, the token face and the bridged WETH token
findings.difference: On Arc the USDC blocklist lives in the Native Coin Control precompile and the EVM checks it on every value-bearing call, so a listed address can neither send nor receive the native asset. The ERC-20 face of USDC moves the same balance and fails the same check. The bridged WETH token of the CrossChainTokenService asks the same list on every transfer through an adapter contract. On Ethereum a USDC blacklist entry stops USDC only, and ETH and WETH keep moving.
findings.mechanism: 1. The USDC blacklister (0x2a2b7ff330f15f9a8c52af5fec27d775f5138467) lists the PoolManager address. In the simulation this is one storage entry of 0x1800000000000000000000000000000000000001, the entry for the PoolManager address in the mapping at slot 2, set to 1 by state override. 2. A native payout, which take performs as a value call from the PoolManager (src/types/Currency.sol:44-52), reverts with 'Blocked address', so take of address(0) reverts, and collectProtocolFees for address(0) uses the same call (src/ProtocolFees.sol:56). 3. USDC.transfer from the PoolManager reverts, so take of 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 reverts (src/types/Currency.sol:60-86). 4. A value call into the PoolManager reverts before its code runs, and USDC.transfer to the PoolManager reverts, so settle can credit nothing under either id (src/PoolManager.sol:349-364). 5. WETH.transfer from the PoolManager and to the PoolManager reverts with AccountDenylisted(PoolManager), because the token calls isDenylisted on the adapter 0x3ebe1f103151890346cd7dbcec1c596cc50ef58e, which reads the USDC blocklist. 6. EURC and cirBTC keep moving, since each has its own list. Swaps and liquidity changes that are settled with ERC-6909 claims alone still run, and nothing in the three affected currencies can enter or leave.
findings.impact: At block 32,769,037 the PoolManager held 2,442,363 USDC of native balance for both ids and 9.54 bridged WETH. Of the 286,916 Initialize logs that cycle 4 collected up to block 32,670,244, 229,191 name 0x3600, 53,208 name address(0) and 275 name the WETH token. Every liquidity provider, swapper and claim holder in those pools loses access for as long as the entry stands. The source has no path that pays out without the transfer (src/PoolManager.sol:291-297).
findings.preconditions: The USDC blacklister, a Circle role, must list the PoolManager address. An ordinary account cannot write the list. The effect was reproduced with eth_call and a state override, with the PoolManager as an inner caller, and no transaction was sent. I could not read the WETH implementation source, which is unverified, so the claim about WETH rests on the access list of a transfer and on the simulated reverts.
findings.mitigations: Deployers and interfaces should state that on Arc the bridged WETH token shares the USDC blocklist, so one decision of one issuer covers native USDC, its token face and WETH. Liquidity providers who want an asset outside that list can use EURC or cirBTC, which carry their own issuer lists. Nothing in core can route around a listed PoolManager address.

cleared.check: Faces angle on Arc, with the moves earlier models left out. One caller, three ids over one balance (address(0) in wei, the token face 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000000 in units of 10^12 wei, the USDC implementation address 0xc6ad664ac6679f4ce74e10e91449c93ec1ae3ca6), sync before and inside the unlock, settle, take, mint, burn, payment through the face, native value forced in by SELFDESTRUCT, a payout to the PoolManager itself, and collectProtocolFees through the fee adapter that any account can call.
cleared.result: No order gains more than one face unit minus one wei per settle, which is less than 0.000001 USDC. On chain at block 32,767,874: (a) 752,591,764,406 wei forced in after sync of the face raised the reading by one unit and settle credited 1 unit, a gain of 247,408,235,594 wei; (b) with the balance on a unit boundary, a native take of 1 wei lowered the face reading by one whole unit, and after a new sync 1 wei forced in was credited as 1 unit; (c) collect of the face through the adapter while the face is synced reverted with ProtocolFeeCurrencySynced, collect of 1 wei of native fees was allowed (src/ProtocolFees.sol:49 exempts address(0)) and lowered the face reading by one unit, after which settle reverted with a panic on the subtraction at src/PoolManager.sol:360; (d) with the implementation address synced, collect of the face was allowed and settle panicked the same way; (e) take of the face with the PoolManager as recipient left the balance unchanged, settle credited 0 and the caller kept the debit; (f) a native take to the PoolManager and any take under the implementation id reverted, also for amount 0. Fee collection therefore only lowers a reading inside a bracket. It gives the caller a free way to place the balance just below a unit boundary, where earlier models needed a native debit of 1 wei. A bounded search over a model with the unit scaled to 4 base units (4,062,481 states at depth 10, fee collection and forced value included) found a best gain of 3 base units with one settle and 6 with two, that is one unit minus one base unit per settle. Each such settle needs a value-bearing call for the forced wei, which costs at least 9,000 gas, 1.8 * 10^14 wei at the 20 gwei fee floor, against a gain below 10^12 wei. Pool operations and hook deltas move amounts inside one currency id and add no cross id move, so they were left out of the model.
cleared.source: eth_call with state overrides via https://arc.drpc.org at block 32,767,874 (research/network-risk/cycles/007/stablecoin-l1.work/a1_faces.py), model in research/network-risk/cycles/007/stablecoin-l1.work/a4_model.py, src/PoolManager.sol:279-297 and 349-364, src/ProtocolFees.sol:44-57, https://docs.arc.io/arc/references/evm-differences.md (20 gwei floor)

cleared.check: Critic gap of cycle 6: the code of the Arc fee adapter and of the jar it pays. Can an ordinary account choose the recipient of a fee collection, receive the fees, or re-enter the PoolManager through the payout while it is unlocked.
cleared.result: No. collect has no caller check and passes the immutable TOKEN_JAR as recipient, so the caller chooses only currency and amount. The jar has an empty receive function, so the native payout of src/types/Currency.sol:48 runs no code that calls back. The jar pays out only through release, which requires the releaser, a WormholeReleaser contract under the same governance path as the PoolManager owner. triggerFeeUpdate lets any account push the fee that the pool override or the policy gives, and src/ProtocolFees.sol:37 caps it at 1000 pips per direction. With amount 0 and a currency without accrued fees the adapter makes the PoolManager call transfer(jar, 0) on an address of the caller's choice, which is the zero amount shape of P2 without an unlock and moves nothing.

cleared.check: Pooled assets angle on Arc: for native USDC under both ids, EURC, cirBTC and bridged WETH, does transfer or balanceOf do anything a holder can trigger (rebase, fee, callback, share accounting, special amounts), and does a transfer write a counter or a flow limit for the sender. This is the Arc part of L-306, answered with access lists because no endpoint served debug_traceCall.
cleared.result: No such behaviour. A transfer out of the PoolManager touches only the two balances, the pause flag, proxy slots and, for USDC and WETH, the blocklist read. The same slots appear for an amount of 1, for the whole balance and for one third to a second recipient, and no slot is specific to the sender apart from its balance. USDC keeps no balance in storage and moves native value through the Native Coin Authority precompile. EURC and cirBTC share the FiatToken implementation 0xc6061272419bb754a6c0386d1df81ddb3fe5cf3c and keep balance and blacklist state in the mapping at slot 9. The WETH implementation is unverified. Of its 46 selectors I could name 33 (ERC-20, permit, pause, minter and ownership functions, service, tokenId, denylistProvider and isDenylisted) and 13 remain unnamed, and one global slot that every transfer reads holds zero and could not be named; a follow-up lead covers both. In the coupling test a transfer of one third of each balance left every other reading unchanged except the known USDC implementation mirror. Cycle 4 took and repaid the full balance of each of the four tokens 3 and 25 times in a row without a change in behaviour.
cleared.source: eth_createAccessList, eth_getStorageAt and eth_call via https://arc.drpc.org at blocks 32,767,960 and 32,769,037 (research/network-risk/cycles/007/stablecoin-l1.work/a2_access.py and f1_coupling.py)

cleared.check: Arc part of L-321: are entries of the Denylist at 0x3600000000000000000000000000000000000004 added by rules from observed behaviour, so that an ordinary account could make the PoolManager meet a rule with zero amount or dust native takes.
cleared.result: No. The contract writes an entry only when a denylister calls denylist(address[]), denylisters are named by the owner, and the node's pool validator only reads the list for the sender, the to address and EIP-7702 authorities of a transaction. No part of the client source I read adds entries. The PoolManager and its periphery are not listed today. A listing of the PoolManager would be a governance action already recorded as F-052.

cleared.check: Can an ordinary account sign for the PoolManager at the USDC token, through permit, transferWithAuthorization or an ERC-1271 check, and so move the native balance without a take.
cleared.result: No. The signature paths of the token need a signature of the owner of the funds. The PoolManager has no private signer, and its code has no isValidSignature function and no fallback (src/PoolManager.sol:80-395), so a contract signature check against it fails. The PoolManager never calls approve on any token (src/types/Currency.sol:40-88 holds its only token calls).
cleared.source: src/PoolManager.sol:80-395, src/types/Currency.sol:40-104 and the token implementation source cited in cycle 2 (https://sourcify.dev/server/v2/contract/5042/0xc6ad664ac6679f4ce74e10e91449c93ec1ae3ca6?fields=sources,abi,compilation)

cleared.check: L-264: walk sync, a slot clearing action and settle with the StorageCredits precompile 0x1060000000000000000000000000000000000000 as currency on the deployed PoolManager, and test every way the credit could leave.
cleared.result: The credit is one unit per cleared slot and can only become an ERC-6909 claim. At block 50,460,341, with a measuring stub at an address that holds 230,765 units of pathUSD claims: balanceOf(PoolManager) at the precompile was 13 before, sync stored 13, a burn of the claims inside the unlock cleared one slot and the reading was 14 at once, settle returned 1 and the caller's delta under the precompile id was 1. take of that id reverted for amounts 1 and 0, because the precompile answers transfer with UnknownFunctionSelector (0xaa4bc69a). transfer, transferFrom and approve sent to the precompile by an ordinary caller reverted the same way. mint of 1 claim under the id closed the delta and the unlock returned. No real asset is accounted under that id. The gas side of the lead was answered in cycle 4: creating a slot costs 245,000 gas more when no credit is left, any account can use the credits up, and no call fails for it.

cleared.check: L-197: what the v1.18.2 item EVM call input hardening and the v1.18.4 fix for EVM execution changed, and whether the PoolManager's call and return data sequences depend on it.
cleared.result: v1.18.2 introduced evm2 with a patch that passes call input as a borrowed range of the caller's memory. At the mainnet revision the range is resolved through the caller frame on each read, so growth of the child's memory cannot corrupt it, and output is written to the caller's memory after the child has ended. v1.18.4 added a check that the remaining gas covers the input cost before a precompile or the T14 account marker copies its input, in crates/precompiles/src/lib.rs and crates/evm/src/instructions.rs, and changed no other module of the seven execution crates I compared. The PoolManager's calls use disjoint input and output ranges for transfer (src/types/Currency.sol:73), no output range for hooks (src/libraries/Hooks.sol:134) and Solidity's same range pattern for balanceOf (src/types/Currency.sol:94). A differential of 32 cases that cover these three patterns, a child that grows its memory and a second call after the memory was rewritten matched revm byte for byte. Cycle 4 established that the jit feature is absent from the default build and that 256 swaps and 288 adds through the deployed bytecode matched the source formulas. Not confirmed: which features each validator compiles in.

leadResults.answer: Both changes are identified. v1.18.2 moved from revm 43.0.3 to evm2 with a patch that passes call input as a borrowed range of the caller's memory; at the mainnet revision 66687c18 the range is resolved through the caller frame on each read. v1.18.4 changed two files with identical dependencies: the precompile provider and the T14 account marker instruction now check that the remaining gas covers the input cost before they copy the borrowed input. Neither touches return data or transient storage handling. A 32 case differential on nested calls with overlapping input and output ranges matched revm byte for byte. The jit feature is outside the default build (cycle 4). Not confirmed: the build features of each validator.

No call site exists at commit 697ea97. committed_copy and call_tx do not occur in 351 modules of 13 node crates, transact is used only by tests and by the prewarming worker on a separate EVM, and precompiles cannot call contracts.
